title: Eardrum puncture (myringotomy)
what: The doctor makes a tiny opening in the eardrum. Pus or fluid drains out of the ear through it.
why: For a severe ear infection when pus presses on the eardrum and pain does not ease, or when fluid stays behind the eardrum for a long time.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes a few minutes
tell_doctor: Allergy to painkillers or numbing medicine
For a child: how long it has hurt and how high the fever is

prepare.title: Numbing
prepare.text: It is usually done with local numbing, and sometimes under anesthesia for children. Your doctor will say.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: If there will be anesthesia, the clinic will tell you when to stop eating.

steps: The ear is numbed with drops or a shot
The patient sits or lies down, and the head is held still
Using a funnel or microscope, the doctor finds the eardrum
A tiny opening is made with a thin needle
The fluid or pus is suctioned out
A cotton ball is placed in the ear
feel: There may be a brief sharp pain or a pop
Afterward, pain from the pressure usually eases quickly
Discharge from the ear in the first days
after: Keep the ear dry until your doctor says it is OK
Use drops and medicines as prescribed
The opening usually heals on its own in a few days
red_flags: The fever stays or rises, or a severe headache
Swelling and pain behind the ear
Severe dizziness, or a drooping face: see a doctor urgently

faq.a: Usually not. The opening is tiny and heals on its own.

faq.q: Why not wait for it to burst on its own?
faq.a: A neat opening made by the doctor heals better than a tear.

reminders.text: Ear procedure in 2 hours. Bring your medicine list.
